we have studied the fast protonic conductivity and proton dynamics in the fast ionic conductor Cs5H 3 (SO4)4·H2O by 1H NMR spectroscopy and found that the proton dynamics in this system is dominated by fast proton transfer in the high-temperature phase.

the fast protonic conductivity of Cs 5 H3(SO4 ) 4 H2O above 414 K is due to the motion of protons of the acid group, which is coupled to the motion of the crystal water molecule, while the proton NMR linewidth transitions at 240 and 300 K are due to the slowing down of protonic motion in the acid groups and crystal water reorientational dynamics.
the protonic conductivity in the superionic phase is caused by the motion of acid hydrogen atoms, while the crystal water protons are not mobile.

we have demonstrated the existence of fast ionic conductivity in the Cs5H3 (SO4)4·H2O compound, which is the first example of fast ionic conduction in a non-hydrous protonic conductor.
